outline: 1844 Finding Unknown Sides Given the Area

examples.solution_text:
(a) Segment $h$ meets base $a$ at the marked right angle, so $h$ is its perpendicular height.
(b) Yes. Sides $a$ and $c$ are parallel, so $h$ is perpendicular to both. Side $s$ is slanted and does not meet either base at $90^{\circ}$.

The height runs from the opposite vertex $R$ to the line containing base $PQ$.
Extend $PQ$ to the marked right angle. Segment $t$ is the matching height, even though it is outside the triangle.

(a) Side $q$ meets base $p$ at $90^{\circ}$, so $q$ is the height.
(b) Side $p$ meets base $q$ at $90^{\circ}$, so $p$ is the height.
A side can be the height when it is perpendicular to the chosen base.

Segment $u$ meets the vertical base at the marked right angle and reaches the opposite side.
$u$ is the height. The height is horizontal because the chosen base is vertical.

examples.question_text: A triangle and its chosen base-height pair are turned on the page without changing their size. Does the height change? Explain.
examples.solution_text:
No. Turning the whole triangle preserves its lengths and angles.
The chosen base and its matching height turn together and still meet at $90^{\circ}$. Height does not mean vertical on the page.

Segment $k$ runs from the opposite vertex to base $b$ and meets it at the marked right angle.
$k$ is its perpendicular height. Side $s$ is not perpendicular to $b$.

examples.derivation: AB is horizontal at y=0. D=(1.4,2.6) lies on the opposite side, and H=(1.4,0) lies on AB. DH is vertical and therefore perpendicular to AB. The right-angle marker matches these directions. The construction follows lines 1027–1030 and image46; the answer appears only in the solution.

The chosen base AB lies on y=3.4; the opposite side DC lies on y=0. H=(0,0) is on the extension of DC beyond D. AH is vertical, perpendicular to both horizontal side lines, and labelled t. The marker at A correctly shows the right angle. This follows image45 part d and lines 1022–1025.

AB lies on y=x. The perpendicular through C=(4.8,1.2) lies on y=-x+6, meeting the base line at H=(3,3), beyond B=(2.4,2.4). Thus CH is the external matching height. The marker's arms follow CH and HB; its rounded coordinates preserve the right angle. This adapts the extended-base construction in image66 part f and lines 1223–1235.
